Mash the zucchini.
Combine with the yogurt.
Serve at room temperature.
Yogurt moistens the chicken and makes swallowing easier.
Pear mash with lor cheese
Half a cooked pear
Mash the pear.
Mix with the lor cheese.
If the texture is thick, add a little breast milk.
Unsalted lor cheese provides protein and calcium.
Milk semolina porridge (12+ months)
Heat the milk and add the semolina, sprinkling it in like rain.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Before 12 months, make it with breast milk or formula instead of cow’s milk; don’t add sugar.
Sütlaç rice pudding (sugar-free, child)
1 dessert spoon rice flour
Half a banana or 2 dates (pitted, mashed)
Cook the rice in half a cup of water until soft.
Add the milk and bring to the boil.
Loosen the rice flour with a little milk, add it and cook for 10 minutes, stirring.
Sweeten with mashed banana or dates and spoon into bowls.
Use fruit instead of sugar as a sweetener.
Banana mash with kefir (12+ months)
3 tablespoons plain kefir
Mix with the kefir.
Don’t use flavoured or sweetened kefir.
Plain kefir contains probiotics.
Egg mash with cheese (12+ months)
1 hard-boiled egg
1 tablespoon low-salt white cheese (soaked in water)
Soak the cheese in water for 1 hour to remove the salt.
Mash the egg.
Mix with the cheese and olive oil.
Serve spread on bread.
Soaking the cheese in water reduces the salt.
Ayran (child, unsalted)
Whisk the yogurt with water.
Whisk until frothy.
Pour into a glass and serve straight away.
Don’t add salt.
Unsalted ayran goes well with meals.
Banana yogurt smoothie (child)
Blend all the ingredients.
Don’t add honey or sugar.
Drinking through a thick straw supports muscle development.
Strawberry milk (sugar-free)
4 ripe strawberries
Wash the strawberries and remove the stalks.
Blend with the milk.
Strain if you wish.
If strawberry is being given for the first time, watch for allergy.
Homemade apple juice (diluted)
Peel and chop the apple.
Strain and cool.
Give at most half a cup a day.
Whole fruit should be preferred to fruit juice; keep the daily amount limited.
Apricot compote (sugar-free)
6 dried apricots (unsulphured)
Wash the apricots and soak in water for 2 hours.
Cook in the same water for 15 minutes.
Cool and serve the liquid with the chopped apricots.
Chop the apricot pieces small.
Choose unsulphured (dark-coloured) apricots.
Oat milk (homemade, 12+ months)
3 cups cold drinking water
Soak the oats in water for 15 minutes and drain.
Blend with fresh water for 30 seconds.
Strain through muslin.
Store in the fridge.
Plant milks don’t replace cow’s milk and shouldn’t be given as the main drink.
Linden tea (child, sugar-free)
1 dessert spoon linden flowers
Add the linden and turn off the heat.
Steep for 5 minutes and strain.
Cool to lukewarm and give half a tea glass.
Don’t give herbal teas to young children often or in large amounts; if they take medication, consult a doctor.
Unsalted menemen (child)
1 tomato (peeled)
A quarter green pepper
Soften the pepper in butter.
Cook the grated tomato for 5 minutes.
Add the egg and stir until fully cooked.
Cool to lukewarm and serve with bread.
The egg must be fully cooked; don’t add salt.
Bulgur pilaf with zucchini and tomato (child)
Half a cup of coarse pilaf bulgur
Dice the zucchini small and toss in butter for 2 minutes.
Add the bulgur and water and cook until the water is absorbed.
Let it rest for 10 minutes and serve.
Make it without salt; the family’s portion can be salted separately.
Baked chicken and vegetables (child)
1 chicken thigh (boneless)
Dice the chicken and vegetables small and toss with oil and thyme.
Bake in a covered oven dish for 35 minutes.
Check the chicken is fully cooked and let it cool to lukewarm.
Cooking covered keeps the meat tender.
Mini vegetable pizza (child)
1 tablespoon finely chopped pepper and mushroom
Cut circles from the lavash with a glass.
Add the tomato, vegetables and kashar.
Bake for 8 minutes and let cool to lukewarm.
Don’t add processed meats such as sucuk or salami.
Homemade wholewheat crackers
4 tablespoons water
Knead the ingredients and roll out thinly.
Cut small squares and prick with a fork.
Unsalted crackers are suitable for snacks.
